_comment: S2453. Each entry is the ADDRESS of a timing figure written in prose, never a copy of it.
The number stays in the document in exactly one place; this file only says where to find it
and which telemetry key measures the same thing. A copy here would be a third source of
truth and the same silent-divergence defect one level down.
pattern: must match its document EXACTLY once, group 1 = seconds, group 2 = the
foreground/background verdict the prose promises. A prose sentence that states the verdict as
its surrounding section rather than as a word beside the number declares it in 'verdict'
instead - that copies a binary, not a measurement. A reworded line breaks the anchor and the
gate answers 'cannot verify' rather than green.

claims.note: The whole fast-gate batch as the caller waits on it. This is the row that went ~7x stale in silence between 2026-08-01 and 2026-09-03.
Only journalled when the batch is run with -IncludeDetekt, so this claim is often below the sample floor and reports 'no telemetry' instead of a verdict.
Rule 6 itself. This copy is the one that actually decides: CLAUDE.md is in context on every turn, so a stale figure here is read far more often than the table it was copied from.
The same figure restated for non-Claude agents. Listed separately because it is a separate hand-written copy and drifts on its own.
